activities.title: A* vs BFS: same goal, different work
activities.objective: Compare frontier ordering, explored work, and shortest-path behavior for BFS and A* on the same maze.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response distinguishes search work from path quality, connects the heuristic to frontier ordering, and avoids claiming that A* is always faster.

activities.title: Why local search gets stuck or escapes
activities.objective: Compare one local-search trajectory or matched seeded restarts, separating reliability from final and best solution cost.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response connects the acceptance rule to the trajectory, verifies equivalent starts and restart counts, and explains why success frequency and mean cost can rank algorithms differently.

activities.title: Safe, risky, or unknown?
activities.objective: Use percept evidence to distinguish a square that is proven safe, possibly hazardous, or unresolved.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response distinguishes unknown from dangerous, separates entailment from plausibility, and does not treat a probability estimate as proof of safety.

activities.title: SAT, UNSAT, or entailed?
activities.objective: Convert a knowledge base to CNF, inspect DPLL or CDCL evidence, and explain any learned clause and backjump without overclaiming solver fidelity.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response distinguishes satisfiability from entailment, traces decisions and implication reasons, and justifies why a learned clause is valid and its non-chronological backjump level is safe.

activities.title: Base rates and false alarms
activities.objective: Connect prior prevalence, true positives, false positives, and posterior probability.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response explains why the posterior depends on both test quality and the prior/base rate, and does not equate accuracy or sensitivity with the probability of the condition after a positive result.

activities.title: Explaining away
activities.objective: Predict and explain how evidence for one cause can lower belief in another after conditioning on a common effect.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response compares the before/after posterior and explains the common-effect dependence rather than saying one cause directly suppresses the other.

activities.title: Which neighbors vote—or get averaged?
activities.objective: Compare categorical voting with continuous-target averaging while holding neighbor selection and relevant controls constant.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response identifies the actual nearest neighbors, separates selection from aggregation, and explains why classification votes over labels while regression computes a uniform or distance-weighted mean.

activities.title: Fit the training set, fail the future
activities.objective: Separate training error from validation/test behavior as model capacity changes.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response identifies the point where additional capacity continues to improve training fit while held-out performance stops improving or worsens, and does not define overfitting as simply having a complex model.

activities.title: Why nonlinearity changes capacity
activities.objective: Compare an affine-only network with a nonlinear representation and explain the decision-boundary change.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response explains that stacking affine layers without a nonlinear activation remains affine, then connects nonlinearity to the network's ability to represent a non-linear boundary.

activities.title: Assign, move, repeat
activities.objective: Predict one assignment and centroid update, then explain the alternating k-means cycle.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response separates the assignment step from the centroid-update step, cites distances or membership evidence, and recognizes that initialization can change the final clustering.

activities.title: One convolution cell
activities.objective: Predict one output-cell multiply-and-sum before revealing the feature-map value.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response matches kernel entries to the local image patch, performs or interprets the multiply-and-sum correctly, and distinguishes the filter response from a semantic object label.

activities.title: One Q-update
activities.objective: Predict an action, TD target, and update direction before stepping the learner.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response connects reward, discounted next-state value, current Q-value, and learning rate to the update direction and distinguishes exploration from the learned policy.

activities.title: Same answer, less search
activities.source: existing Guided Challenge + local Quick Assign response layer
activities.objective: Explain why a safe alpha-beta cutoff can reduce evaluated work without changing the minimax result.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response uses the alpha/beta bound to justify why the skipped branch cannot improve the relevant decision and explicitly states that alpha-beta returns the same exact minimax value.

activities.title: Attend, then predict
activities.source: existing Guided Challenge + local Quick Assign response layer
activities.objective: Connect a controlled representation/attention change to the next-token probability distribution.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response cites a specific attention/logit/probability change, distinguishes attention weights from a complete explanation of the prediction, and separates the probability distribution from the generation rule.

activities.title: A proposed call is not an executed action
activities.source: existing Guided Challenge + local Quick Assign response layer
activities.objective: Trace a proposed tool call through validation, authorization, execution, observation, and context update.
activities.teacher_look_for: A strong response distinguishes model output, schema validity, authorization, execution, and observation, and identifies the exact gate where a denied or invalid action stops.
